name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct for EXCAVA. Its MoE design cuts latency 30-40% versus dense models while matching or exceeding their output quality, directly raising capability per second of compute. The trade-off is higher memory bandwidth demand—MoE layers need fast access to expert weights—but the node’s 8xA100 setup with NVLink covers it.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B’s MoE latency claim ignores sharding overhead—EXCAVA’s 8xA100 node can’t feed experts fast enough to hit those numbers. DeepSeek-R1-671B’s dense single-model path locks us into one architecture with no scaling headroom, but it’s the safer bet for now. Run a 24-hour benchmark on both with the same prompt set—if Qwen3’s MoE doesn’t beat R1 by at least 0.5% throughput, we default to R1.
